q-130790.name: Question 2
q-130790.problem: Given that $2x+6=5x$, what is the value of $x?$
q-130790.worked_solution:
We must bring all variables to one side of the equation and all constants to the other side. 

Notice that we have $2x$ on the left-hand side and $5x$ on the right-hand side. Since the variable on the right-hand side has a larger coefficient, let's bring all the variables to this side. 

The first step is to remove the $2x$ from the left-hand side. We do this by subtracting $2x$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+6 & =5x \\ 2x+6-2x & =5x-2x \\ 6 & =3x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides of the equation by $3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}6 & =3x \\ \frac{6}{3} & =\frac{3x}{3} \\ 2 & =\frac{\cancel{3}x}{\cancel{3}} \\ 2 & =x \\ x & =2\end{aligned}
$$

q-181274.name: Question 3
q-181274.worked_solution:
We must bring all variables to one side of the equation and all constants to the other side. 

Notice that we have $10x$ on the left-hand side and $6x$ on the right-hand side. Since the variable on the left-hand side has a larger coefficient, let's bring all the variables to this side.

The first step is to remove the $6x$ from the right-hand side of the equation. We do this by subtracting $6x$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}10x-3 & =5+6x \\ 10x-3-6x & =5+6x-6x \\ 4x-3 & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we remove the $-3$ from the left-hand side. We do this by adding $3$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-3 & =5 \\ 4x-3+3 & =5+3 \\ 4x & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides of the equation by $4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4x & =8 \\ \frac{4x}{4} & =\frac{8}{4} \\ \frac{\cancel{4}x}{\cancel{4}} & =2 \\ x & =2\end{aligned}
$$

q-181286.name: Question 4
q-181286.worked_solution:
We must bring all variables to one side of the equation and all constants to the other side. 

Notice that we have $-3t$ on the left-hand side and $3t$ on the right-hand side. Since the variable on the right-hand side has a larger coefficient, let's bring all the variables to this side.

The first step is to remove the $-3t$ from the left-hand side of the equation. We do this by adding $3t$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4-3t & =3t-2 \\ -4-3t+3t & =3t-2+3t \\ -4 & =6t-2\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we remove the $-2$ from the right-hand side. We do this by adding $2$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4 & =6t-2 \\ -4+2 & =6t-2+2 \\ -2 & =6t\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides of the equation by $6:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-2 & =6t \\ \frac{(-2)}{6} & =\frac{6t}{6} \\ -\frac{1}{3} & =\frac{\cancel{6}t}{\cancel{6}} \\ -\frac{1}{3} & =t \\ t & =-\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

q-128811.name: Question 5
q-128811.worked_solution:
First, we expand the parentheses on both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3(1-p) & =4(p+1) \\ -3\cdot 1+3\cdot p & =4\cdot p+4\cdot 1 \\ -3+3p & =4p+4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we must bring all variables to one side of the equation and all constants to the other side. 

Notice that we have $3p$ on the left-hand side and $4p$ on the right-hand side. Since the variable on the right-hand side has a larger coefficient, let's bring all the variables to this side. 

The first step is to remove the $3p$ from the left-hand side of the equation. We do this by subtracting $3p$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3+3p & =4p+4 \\ -3+3p-3p & =4p+4-3p \\ -3 & =p+4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we remove the $4$ from the right-hand side. We do this by subtracting $4$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3 & =p+4 \\ -3-4 & =p+4-4 \\ -7 & =p \\ p & =-7\end{aligned}
$$

q-128811.html:
Question 5
?

If −3(1−p)=4(p+1), then p=

a
−16
b
−7
c
−14
d
34
e
1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we expand the parentheses on both sides: −3(1−p)=4(p+1)−3⋅1+3⋅p=4⋅p+4⋅1−3+3p=4p+4

Now, we must bring all variables to one side of the equation and all constants to the other side.

Notice that we have 3p on the left-hand side and 4p on the right-hand side. Since the variable on the right-hand side has a larger coefficient, let's bring all the variables to this side.

The first step is to remove the 3p from the left-hand side of the equation. We do this by subtracting 3p from both sides: −3+3p=4p+4−3+3p−3p=4p+4−3p−3=p+4

Finally, we remove the 4 from the right-hand side. We do this by subtracting 4 from both sides:

−3=p+4−3−4=p+4−4−7=pp=−7

q-171587.name: Question 6
q-171587.worked_solution:
First, we expand the parentheses on both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}7(x-2) & =3(x+2)+2x \\ 7\cdot x-7\cdot 2 & =3\cdot x+3\cdot 2+2x \\ 7x-14 & =3x+6+2x \\ 7x-14 & =6+3x+2x \\ 7x-14 & =6+5x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we must bring all variables to one side of the equation and all constants to the other side. 

Notice that we have $7x$ on the left-hand side and $5x$ on the right-hand side. Since the variable on the right-hand side has a larger coefficient, let's bring all the variables to this side.

The first step is to remove the $5x$ from the right-hand side of the equation. We do this by subtracting $5x$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}7x-14 & =6+5x \\ 7x-14-5x & =6+5x-5x \\ 2x-14 & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we remove the $-14$ from the left-hand side. We do this by adding $14$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-14 & =6 \\ 2x-14+14 & =6+14 \\ 2x & =20\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides of the equation by $2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =20 \\ \frac{2x}{2} & =\frac{20}{2} \\ \frac{\cancel{2}x}{\cancel{2}} & =10 \\ x & =10\end{aligned}
$$
